headline: WPP keeps most of Coca-Cola's global media business, with Omnicom taking North America
why: A major account review reshapes which agency networks run a global brand's media across Asia Pacific, with new arrangements from 1 December 2026.

idea: Move from one-off posts to longer creator partnerships.

idea: Plan across few platforms and go deep rather than spreading thin.

headline: TikTok leads daily engagement at 1 hour 39 minutes a day; YouTube leads session length

idea: Check data readiness before committing to AI-led campaigns.

why: Consumers are tightening spending despite subsidies, and total retail sales growth slowed to 2.5% year on year.

why: Circana says a larger share of goods is now sold on promotion, and growth varies by category and channel.
idea: Test promotional price points carefully and lead with value, not discounts alone.

why: Consumers start product research on social media, but platform preferences differ by market.
idea: Pair Facebook and Instagram content with WhatsApp for direct follow-up in Malaysia.

headline: Thailand has about 56.6 million social media users, and LINE is a key local platform
why: Social media is a research step before purchase, and Google still leads search in Thailand.
idea: Combine TikTok content with a LINE offer so discovery and purchase sit in one journey.

headline: Grab x Merdeka 2026 runs a month-long Malaysian food promotion with Chef Wan
why: A multi-brand national-pride promotion shows how local food can anchor a festive campaign.
idea: Anchor a festive snack moment around a local chef or food creator.

why: A co-branded character collaboration extends a children's brand into menu items and in-store experiences.
idea: Test a co-branded character collab with in-store activations for a limited run.

why: Humour built on a familiar local dish gives a strong, shareable take on national taste.

why: A gap between where marketers invest and where audiences spend time suggests budgets may be misallocated.
idea: Test budget shifts toward Instagram and YouTube alongside TikTok for Australian launches.

why: TikTok reaches 56.6 million accounts in Thailand, the largest ad-reachable audience of any platform in the report.
idea: Lead Thai short-form creative on TikTok, with Facebook as the second placement.

headline: Thai household spending rises to 21,217 baht a month, led by transport and food
why: Transport costs rose most, and food remains the largest category at 8,342 baht a month, per Commerce Ministry data.
idea: Lead Thai value messaging with food and everyday-essentials offers while fuel costs stay high.

headline: Shopping-centre sales grow led by food; outer-suburban centres weakest at 3.9%
why: Mortgage pressure is weighing on outer-suburban shoppers, even where population growth is strongest.
idea: Plan Australian food and everyday-occasion creative with outer-suburban reach in mind.

why: Higher handouts may lift spending at value retailers, while plantations and e-commerce face new costs.
idea: Time value-pack and everyday-essentials messaging to the handout payout window.

headline: About 80% of regular Malaysian TikTok users go to the app to learn, connect with culture and manage stress
why: A Kearney survey of over 1,000 Malaysians shows TikTok is used for purpose, not only entertainment.
idea: Pair entertainment creative on TikTok with learning or wellbeing angles for Malaysian audiences.

headline: TikTok reaches 55% of Thais for news, and has overtaken Facebook among under-25s
why: Reuters Institute's Digital News Report 2026 finds short-form video is often the first step before YouTube and search.
idea: Use short-form video as the entry point for Thai campaigns, then extend to longer YouTube content.

headline: 72% of marketers plan to raise AI use, but only 45% feel confident applying it successfully
why: The confidence gap is wider than adoption, and measurement is weak in Singapore and Thailand.
idea: Show measurement and AI training in client briefs before promising AI-led results.

headline: Bursa Malaysia ends higher as FBM KLCI reclaims the 1,600 mark
why: The rebound in Malaysia's main equity index is the lead market story this week.
idea: Brief the team on which consumer stocks move with sentiment before timing spend-led creative.

headline: Australian household spending was flat in August 2026, with fuel up 8.1% and spending excluding fuel down 0.3%
why: Fuel is propping up spending while ANZ-Roy Morgan consumer confidence fell 1.5 points to 70.5.
idea: Lead Australian everyday creative with value and fuel-cost reassurance.

headline: Thai Retail Sentiment Index falls 4.9 points to 46.6 in July, with spending per bill down 8.1 points
why: Shoppers are buying fewer items per trip and trading down, while store visits held roughly steady.
idea: Use bundles and smaller pack sizes to keep Thai basket value intact.

why: Analysts expect resilient consumption into year-end, with retail trade up 6.8% year to date through July.
idea: Plan 4Q26 consumer campaigns around resilient spending, with value messaging as a safe default.

idea: Lead Thai everyday creative with value and essentials offers while fuel costs rise.

idea: Keep outdoor activations paused until haze conditions improve.

idea: Show Thai shoppers a clear value case against cheap imported alternatives.

headline: Australia’s inflation rate rises to 4.3 per cent
why: Rising prices and expected RBA rate action squeeze household budgets, so value messaging matters more.
idea: Lead Australian everyday creative with value and reassurance while inflation rises.

headline: The economic outlook for 2027 is stark. Ordinary workers will wear the costs
why: ABC analysis points to a likely rate rise and job cuts, which is likely to keep shoppers cautious into 2027.
idea: Plan 2027 budgets around cautious, value-led consumer spending.

headline: Malaysia faces billions in 1MDB losses even if further recovery efforts succeed, Parliament told
why: The national finance debate in Parliament is the lead Malaysian story this week.
idea: Keep brand messaging clear of political and fiscal headlines this week.

headline: Ringgit ends higher against greenback on confidence in Malaysia’s fundamentals
why: A firmer ringgit and AI-related investment optimism support sentiment for Malaysian consumer brands.
idea: Brief the team on import-linked cost assumptions before locking Q4 pricing.

why: Haze remains the lead Singapore story, keeping outdoor creative a sensitive choice.
idea: Keep outdoor-activation creative paused until haze guidance is clear.

why: Lower haze readings on 27 October may ease outdoor restrictions, but conditions are still changing.
idea: Check NEA PSI readings daily before booking outdoor activations.
